nodes.text: Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that in any $A\subset \mathbb{Z}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=n$ there exists some sum-free subset $B\subseteq A$ with $\lvert B\rvert \geq f(n)$, so that there are no solutions to\[a+b=c\]with $a,b,c\in B$. Estimate $f(n)$.

#792 : [Er65] [Er73] [Er92c] [Va99,1.22] additive combinatorics Erdős [Er65] gave a simple proof that shows $f(n) \geq n/3$. Alon and Kleitman [AlKl90] improved this to $f(n)\geq \frac{n+1}{3}$, and Bourgain [Bo97] further improved this to $\frac{n+2}{3}$. The best lower bound known is\[f(n)\geq \frac{n}{3}+c\log\log n\]for some constant $c>0$, due to Bedert [Be25b] . The best upper bound known is\[f(n) \leq \frac{n}{3}+o(n),\]due to Eberhard, Green, and Manners [EGM14] . This problem is Problem 1 on Green's open problems list .
